item.title: Leading Bank Expands Internal Defensive Security Team with Detection Engineers
item.description:
Leading Bank Expands Internal Defensive Security Team with Detection Engineers

A leading bank is appointing Detection Engineers to join a growing internal defensive security team, transitioning detection engineering from a secondary responsibility within the Cloud function to a specialist, full-time discipline.

🔍 Overview

The role is focused on defensive security and threat hunting, prioritizing the creation of high-quality detections over increasing volume. The position is part of a global team operating across the UK, Poland, and Mexico.

⚙️ Key Details

Responsibilities:

  • Develop high-quality detection use cases utilizing internal security data and external threat intelligence.
  • Translate intelligence into effective detections for the organization.
  • Use Red Team outputs to identify gaps, understand attack techniques, and determine where to detect malicious activity.
  • Conduct threat hunting to identify opportunities for improved defensive coverage.
  • Optimize detection capability by working with technology and security teams.
  • Deliver engineering through Scrum, Agile, and sprint-based ways of working.

Requirements:

  • 3-5 years of experience in security, development, or technology operations.
  • Hands-on experience in writing and developing security detections.
  • Proficiency in threat hunting and defensive security.
  • Experience translating threat intelligence into actionable detections.
  • Background working in a large financial services organization or a similarly complex, highly regulated environment.
  • Comfort working within an Agile/Scrum delivery environment.

🚀 Availability

  • Role: Contractor
  • Location: Sheffield or London (1-2 days per week onsite)
  • Contract Length: Initial 6-month contract
  • Rate: £600 per day via umbrella (Inside IR35)

#Cybersecurity #DetectionEngineering #ThreatHunting #DefensiveSecurity #Banking

Source: Jobs in London

item.title: SpaceXAI Releases Grokipedia v0.3 Update with New Design Tweaks
item.description:
SpaceXAI Releases Grokipedia v0.3 Update with New Design Tweaks

SpaceXAI has released a v0.3 update for Grokipedia, its AI-powered competitor to Wikipedia. The update introduces a new logo and visual refreshes to the homepage, article pages, and live edits page, following a period where the site recently resumed incorporating edits.

⚙️ Key details

Benji Taylor, head of design at SpaceXAI, describes the update as a “newly refreshed Grokipedia.” The v0.3 release follows a development timeline that began with v0.1 in late October 2025, which used AI-cloned pages from Wikipedia, and a v0.2 update a month later. While a Lawfare report in August stated that no entry had changed in more than three months, the site has recently started updating again.

🎨 Visual and Functional Changes

  • Homepage: Previously consisting of a logo and search bar, the new homepage now includes:
    • A list of featured articles featuring digital representations of books that can be spun around.
    • A most-read articles section utilizing a horizontally-scrolling shelf of “book” spines.
    • A tracker for “latest edits.”
  • Live Edits Page: Updated to allow users to see more recent changes at once.
  • Article Pages: Now feature smaller spacing between lines of text and a redesigned format for the key facts tables located at the top of articles.

#SpaceXAI #Grokipedia #AI #Wikipedia

Source: Elon Musk’s Grokipedia has a ‘newly refreshed’ design

item.title: Ubicloud Launches Open Source Cloud for Bare Metal Providers
item.description:
Ubicloud Launches Open Source Cloud for Bare Metal Providers

Ubicloud is an open source cloud that can run anywhere, providing IaaS cloud features on bare metal providers including AWS Bare Metal, Leaseweb, and Hetzner.

🔍 Overview

Ubicloud offers an open source alternative to traditional cloud services to reduce costs and return infrastructure control to the user. The project aims to implement 10% of cloud services that account for 80% of consumption.

🧩 How it works

Ubicloud utilizes a control plane to manage a data plane that leverages open source software. The control plane is responsible for cloudifying bare metal Linux machines.

Component Technical Implementation
Elastic Compute Control plane communicates with Linux bare metal servers using SSH
Virtual Machine Monitor Cloud Hypervisor, with each instance contained in Linux namespaces
Networking IPsec tunneling for encrypted private networks
Firewalls & Load Balancers Linux nftables
Block Storage Storage Performance Development Toolkit (SPDK)

⚙️ Key details

  • Networking: Supports dual-stack IPv4 and IPv6 with both public and private networking. Ubicloud assigns IPv6 addresses to VMs, or users can add IPv4 addresses leased from their provider to the control plane. Each customer’s VMs operate in their own networking namespace.
  • Storage: Non-replicated block storage is provided via SPDK, which allows for future implementation of replication and snapshots. Data encryption keys are encrypted following security best practices.
  • Access Control: Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) allows for the definition of roles, attributes, and permissions for fine-grained resource access.

🚀 Availability

Users can set up Ubicloud themselves on supported providers or use a managed service. The managed cloud is approximately 3x cheaper than AWS.

#Ubicloud #OpenSource #IaaS #CloudComputing #BareMetal

Source: ubicloud/ubicloud
